edges.effect_quant: Different designs and subgroups point in different directions, so a single pooled estimate is not the right way to read this edge.
edges.mechanism: Mood effects from DHEA would likely run through neurosteroid signaling and indirect endocrine changes rather than through a strong antidepressant mechanism.
edges.summary: For depression, the most useful starting point is the 2008 Kritz-Silverstein rct in J Am Geriatr Soc. It found that dhea supplementation produces mixed findings across studies, and the follow-on evidence is broadly consistent even when absolute benefit or harm is modest.
edges.caveats: Subgroup differences, dose thresholds, and competing mechanisms likely explain why the literature does not settle into one clean direction.
